items.proposed_content: The Stirling-motivated oscillatory phase enlarges the shifted-zeta integral into a frequency-indexed family whose analytic behavior separates sharply by mode: nonzero frequency is holomorphic farther in w, whereas the zero-frequency member retains a single simple pole at w=1. Frequency therefore acts as an analytic selector between oscillatory continuation and the resonant pole. The proposition states this dichotomy before the kernel estimates, so its exact continuation inequalities and residue sum remain scan-dependent.

items.proposed_content: In the cubic case, uniquely constrained P and Q polynomials complete imprimitive twists so that the d- and n-summation descriptions satisfy two vector functional equations. Their finite dihedral action, together with pole clearing and successive tube convex hulls, gives global continuation and vertical control for corrected building blocks. Finite local identities, two Möbius stages, and character combinations then reconstruct the fundamental-discriminant series; a shifted three-variable residue calculation fixes the seventh-order leading term, and contour inversion produces the cubic moment polynomial.

items.proposed_content: Splitting the raw quadratic-family sum by sign and congruence class and adding gamma completions creates channels on which the coordinate functional equations act as a finite reflection group. After expansion, reciprocity converts the discriminant average into squarefree character series, so only principal characters, equivalently square index products, contribute to the w=1 residue; Euler factorization then isolates the central arithmetic factor. If Conjecture 3.6 identifies the full reflected local divisor, orbit divisibility and scaling supply the geometric factor and the Tauberian step yields the even-moment asymptotic.

items.proposed_content: The initial w=1 residue separates into a holomorphic Euler remainder whose central value is the arithmetic factor and universal zeta diagonals. The zero-frequency stabilizer transports that principal part across the reflected polar arrangement; under Conjecture 2.7, orbit symmetrization and homogeneous divisibility cancellation select the pole order and geometric factor, after which Wiener-Ikehara transfer gives the even zeta-moment asymptotic.

items.proposed_content: For the smoothed cubic moment, continuation and the vertical bound allow a direct contour shift past the order-seven pole, giving the polynomial and an error from the Re(w)=4/5+epsilon line. Removing the smoothing changes the task: a truncated Perron formula introduces endpoint errors controlled by short-interval moments, the left contour must be reflected into absolute convergence, gamma-ratio oscillation supplies a half-power saving, and the remaining parameters are balanced across small- and large-sieve ranges.

items.proposed_content: For each corrected building block, the functional-equation orbit reflects the known w=1 hyperplane to 3s+2w-3=0, leaving w=3/4 as a possible pole after specializing s=1/2, even after other denominator-clearing candidates are removed by two-variable analyticity. Reconstruction of the target fundamental-discriminant series only requires and proves analyticity for Re(w)>4/5 except at w=1; the possible 3/4 term reappears only when the sharper unweighted argument shifts contours farther left in the r-indexed intermediate series.

items.proposed_content: For degrees one through three, the local correction constraints select a unique completed double Dirichlet series, and the resulting finite reflection group produces finitely many overlapping tube regions whose convex hull can propagate continuation globally. From degree four onward, the same source reports both nonuniqueness of the correction data and an infinite functional-equation group whose generated domain does not reach the central moment point before the expected essential-singularity boundary.
